title: My RPG/Multiplayer game - few months dev ~700 hours, Unity (with AI..)
author: Uo98eq99mmo
selftext:
Hi everyone, this is 1 of 3 games I'm currently building with AI. I'm not a coder or developer, you could say a semi-technical micromanager.. My day job is in a completely different industry, but I've been spending 10-12 hours a day on this for the past few months.

I spent much of 2025-26 experimenting with vibe coding, trying to build a business/research platform with a 300 million record database and automated agent-to-agent research,  and a few other projects,  all in last 18+ months i would say  4,000+ hours....  I gave up as the AI wasn't quite capable of what I wanted. Kept waiting for the next better model every few months ...

I switched to gaming few months ago, as that is more interesting to me. I started gaming in the 90s with the usual single players of that era.  Got addicted to Ultima Online in 1998, playing 15 hours a day at university in the UK (9am - 3am...) Then EverQuest in 1999, if anyone remembers dial-up modems.. and AOL...  Never played WoW. Tried Dota briefly, then took a 10+ year break before getting hooked on Elder Scrolls Online around 2014-15, again playing 12+ hours a day despite having two kids and senior full-time job.. Black Desert Online in 2018 was my last serious MMO. Nothing since has really hooked me.

Anyway, this is my new hobby. I'm building 3games, including a top-down Diablo-style ARPG and an FPS..

This one originally started as a browser MMO using Three.js, Supabase, Google Auth, etc. Initially targeting mobile web, but I wasn't happy with the graphics. Tried Unreal, but I find Unity easier to manage with AI, 

Currently I have a playable demo with five areas, vendors, equipment, mounts, etc. I'd say I'm around 65% towards a decent alpha. Might keep it as a smaller multiplayer PvP game rather than a full MMO.

The game - female protagonist, my own direction brief (to AI) of monsters and mobs, and more emphasis on combat, physics and movement. Directional attacks, blocking, guarding, kicks, ragdolls, different stances inspired by For Honor, no iframes, etc. Basically trying to combine the combat mechanics I've enjoyed across different games.  I don't like arcade/cartoony graphics so am going for a more gritty type style.

For the AI haters.. this wasn't a one-shot prompt.. I literally sit at my computer barking orders at AI for 12+ hours a day, going back and forth fixing things. Probably inefficient, but it is what it is :)

For anyone interested in the setup, I'm using an ASUS ROG with 64GB unified memory, plus a separate desktop with an RTX 3060 12GB and 32GB RAM. 3x claude subscriptions $200 plan, as i finish the tokens on each account every 2 days (even with sonnet 5.5 the cheaper models..) plus Codex for additional Q&A,  audits and image generation.  I use Tripo/Meshy for converting images into 3D assets, and planning to use Suno for music.

I will relase the alpha and game for free. Ideally Steam, but their new 45+ day onboarding process is a pain and i haven't been accepted yet through the tax checks...  so probably [itch.io](http://itch.io) in the next week or two, followed by Epic and hopefully Steam.

Anyway... I'm interested to hear what people think. Still plenty to improve, particularly the combat, but it's been a a good few months.

replies.author: BumblebeeAfraid6220
replies.body:
another thing Ive done is had a tool generated and managed by fable

ive spent most of the week ironing out the workflows and discussing problems and having fable run testsa and harnesses then reviewing and testing work. this has helped me to not have to bark constant orders.

Fable runs checks periodically and gives a sitrep

My opinion is AI gamedev isn't a creative role entirely but a c level management role. In the real world nobody is ever going to give my adhd ass a team. But I can make a tireless automated team that does what I tell it for 200 a month.

Fable manages opus devs. That  way we get the thoughtfulness of fable applied to lesser agents.

replies.author: PoisonSD

“They are 4K” doesn’t mean they are good, this matches the asset flips on steam at best, and lacks the characters of those “80s” games, which I also just disagree with. 

WoW looks better then this because it’s stylized, this does just look like an asset flip, the creatures don’t fit the world, the shops don’t seem to fit the world, it looks like it was pieced jankily together. 

One of the most important things you can do as a developer is look at your game objectively, without bias, and I think you need to do that.
